children: John Healey's first speech as U.K. treasury chief gave little away ahead of his first budget on Oct. 28, focusing mainly on growing business investment, Kathleen Brooks at XTB says in a note. "This is one way to boost public sector spending without adding pressure to the national debt, since this spending is outside of Healey's fiscal rules," she says. Healey also reiterated plans for fiscal devolution, which could include a portion of income tax, though details were lacking, Brooks adds. Healey didn't rule out tax increases, which could suggest that taxes will be raised. "However, we think that the fact he is talking about growth... suggests that tax rises in this budget would not help him to reach his mission." (don.forbes@wsj.com)
